title: Pavement deflection
intro:
A pavement engineer will measure the deflection of a road section under a falling-weight load at randomly chosen points. Earlier sections of the same design had a standard deviation of **0.8 mm**. She wants to estimate the mean deflection within **±0.2 mm** at **99 %** confidence.

Find the critical value z and the number of test points she needs. Give the critical value to three decimals and the sample size as a whole number.

Critical.says: That is the 95 % value. 99 % confidence leaves 0.005 in each tail: z_{0.005}.
That is z_{0.01}, with all of α in one tail. A two-sided 99 % margin puts 0.005 in each tail: z_{0.005}.

SampleSizeNeeded.says: You rounded down (or to the nearest whole number). The formula gives 106.2: always round up, or the margin is a little over 0.2 mm.
You used z = 1.960, the 95 % value. For 99 %, z = 2.576.
You forgot to square. n = (z × σ / E)².

hints: 99 % confidence leaves α = 0.01, so 0.005 in each tail: z = stats.norm.ppf(0.995) or qnorm(0.995).
Always round n up to the next whole number.
